title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In this third draft of 'Analysis situs' (June 1986), Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic, combinatorial framework for a tame ('modérée') topology. The data are a set M of 'models' (cells or lieux) with:
- a relation ≤ (face, or closed-inclusion);
- a relation ≪ ('is contained in / lies inside');
- the subset L ⊂ M of points;
- a disjointness relation ‖.
These satisfy axioms ML0–ML5 on p.34; for example ML0 says X≤Y ⇒ X≪Y, and there are lifting, divisibility, minimal-structure and disjunction axioms.

This page builds a canonical 'atelier' (workshop: a category or structured set of figures) out of these data.

1. Let Φ be the set of subsets F ⊂ M such that (a) F is closed (downward saturated) for ≤, and (b) the elements of F are pairwise compatible in the sense of (1) p.24. The image and the next page ('parties fermées', 'figures infinies', 'de type fini') indicate (a) reads 'fermées pour ≤', not 'finies'.
2. Give Φ two relations:
   - ≤ := inclusion;
   - F ≪ G :⇔ ∀X∈F ∃Y∈G with X≪Y. This is the ∀∃ lifting of ≪ to subsets, i.e. the Hoare/lower-powerdomain preorder.
3. Claims about Φ:
   - Φ is an atelier satisfying axioms At L1, At L2, At L3 and At CL (a 'sup' condition).
   - It contains the principal down-sets X̃ = M_{≤X} (X∈M) as elementary figures.
   - The relations induced on M via X ↦ X̃ (≤, ≪, and ‖ induced from figures) are the original ones.
4. Any atelier 'corresponding' to the given structure identifies with a subset 𝓕 ⊂ Φ satisfying:
   - (i) 𝓕 is closed under passing to closed parts: F∈𝓕, G∈Φ, G≤F ⇒ G∈𝓕;
   - (ii) 𝓕 is closed under compatible unions: F,G∈𝓕 with F≍G (F∪G∈Φ, i.e. all elements of F compatible with all of G) ⇒ F∪G∈𝓕.
   - The next page adds (iii): all X̃ (in particular the points {x}) lie in 𝓕. It also shows that finite-type figures force 𝓕 = finite unions of X̃'s, provided every closed part of an X̃ is of finite type.

Purpose. The conclusion on p.36 is that, up to a 'petit flottement' about infinite figures, a tame-topological workshop is equivalent to the poset-like data (M, ≤, ≪, ‖) satisfying the axioms M0–M4. Figures become down-closed, pairwise-compatible sets of cells, as in a face-poset / Alexandrov-topology description of a cell complex.
errors: The transcription's 'finies, pour ≤' should almost certainly be 'fermées pour ≤'. Finiteness is discussed separately on the next page (figures of finite type, infinite figures).

For ≪ on Φ to be a preorder, and for X̃≪Ỹ ⇔ X≪Y, one needs ≪ on M to be transitive and stable under composition with ≤. One direction uses ML0: X'≤X ⇒ X'≪X ≪ Y. The converse X≪Y'≤Y ⇒ X≪Y also needs this. Transitivity is not stated on pp.34–35 and is presumably assumed earlier.
X̃ ∈ Φ requires that any two faces of a single model are compatible. This must follow from the definition (1) on p.24, which is not visible here.
The claim that Φ satisfies At L1–3 and At CL is asserted without proof. The definitions of these axioms are on earlier pages and are not available.

ideas.what: Recovering a space (atelier of figures) from a combinatorial structure on cells: figures = ≤-down-closed, pairwise compatible sets of models; elementary figures = principal down-sets X̃ = M_{≤X}.
ideas.modern_name: Face-poset / Alexandrov-topology description of regular cell complexes; abstract cell complexes; closed subcomplexes as down-sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937, posets/finite spaces); Björner (1984, regular CW complexes via face posets); Kovalevsky (abstract cell complexes, 1989)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, without this formalism

ideas.what: Lifting ≪ from elements to subsets by F≪G iff ∀X∈F ∃Y∈G, X≪Y.
ideas.modern_name: Hoare (lower) powerdomain preorder / Egli–Milner lower half

ideas.what: Characterisation of admissible figure-families 𝓕 ⊂ Φ as down-closed families stable under unions of compatible members, containing all X̃.
ideas.modern_name: Configurations of an event structure / consistent down-closed sets (coherence-space cliques); ideal-completion-like closure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel (1981, event structures); Girard (1987, coherence spaces)

missed.claim: Φ is formally the set of configurations of a prime event structure with binary conflict. Here (M,≤) is the causality order and conflict is non-compatibility; Φ is the set of down-closed, pairwise conflict-free sets. Conditions (i)–(ii) on 𝓕 mirror closure properties of configuration domains (coherent prime-algebraic domains). Grothendieck uses this structure as the combinatorial skeleton of tame topology. No link between his 'ateliers' and domain theory / event structures appears in the literature.
missed.quote: Soit Φ l'ens. des parties de M qui sont a) fermées pour ≤ et b) formées d'éléments deux à deux compatibles … si F ≍ G i.e. F∪G∈Φ … F∪G ∈ 𝓕
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests a dictionary between combinatorial models of stratified/tame spaces and domain-theoretic or concurrency structures. Directed topology already links concurrency and topology, so this resonance is suggestive, though it is a formal parallel rather than a deep result.

missed.claim: The axiomatisation of tame topology via (M, ≤, ≪, ‖) with axioms ML0–ML5 / M0–M4 and the 'atelier' axioms At L1–3, At CL. This is an unpublished foundational framework for the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse, never developed in the literature (o-minimality went another way).
missed.quote: Alors Φ est un atelier satisfaisant At L 1, At L 2, At L 3 et At CL
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This offers an alternative, purely combinatorial-order-theoretic foundation for tame topology to compare with o-minimal structures and with exit-path/stratified approaches.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows an unpublished step in Grothendieck's own axiomatic tame topology: a canonical universal atelier built from down-closed compatible sets of cells. The individual ingredients (face posets, down-sets, Hoare order, consistent configurations) are standard, so the novelty lies in the framework and an unremarked formal parallel with event structures, not in a striking result.
transcription_corrections: 'a) finies, pour ≤' should read 'a) fermées pour ≤'.
'Alors Φ est une relation[?]' should likely read 'Alors Φ est un atelier' (the 'ateliers' crossed out on p.34 and the At-axioms support this).
'comme [-objets-] formes[?] élémentaires' should likely read 'comme figures élémentaires'.
'{+Tout relation correspondante[?] à une+}' should likely read 'Tout atelier correspondant à une …'.
'(i) ∀ F ∈ 𝓕, et G ≤ F … de F, ∈) i.e. G ∈ 𝓕' should read roughly '(i) ∀F∈𝓕 et G≤F (G partie fermée de F, ∈Φ), G∈𝓕'.
